title: Over a local ring in which simple roots of monic polynomials lift, etale algebras with a rational point over the closed point retract
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring such that for every monic $f\in R[T]$ and every $a_0\in\kappa$ with $\overline f(a_0)=0$ and $\overline{f'}(a_0)\neq0$ there is $a\in R$ with $f(a)=0$ and $a\bmod\mathfrak m=a_0$ (simple roots of monic polynomials lift; Stacks' definition of henselian). Let $R\to S$ be a ring map such that $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal lying over $\mathfrak m$ such that the induced map of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] $\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is an isomorphism. Then there is exactly one $R$-algebra homomorphism $\tau:S\to R$ (a retraction of $R\to S$) with $\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), proof of 1=>8 (via Proposition Tag 00UE, etale is locally standard etale, and Lemma Tag 06RR, lemma-uniqueness)

proof.text: *The residue map $\rho$.* Write $\pi:R\to\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$ and $\iota:R\to S$ for the structure map. The composite $\kappa\to S/\mathfrak q\hookrightarrow\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-residue-field] (the residue field of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ at $\mathfrak q$ is the fraction field of the domain $S/\mathfrak q$) is an isomorphism by hypothesis, so the subring $S/\mathfrak q$ contains the image of $\kappa$, which is all of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; hence $R\to S/\mathfrak q$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak m$, and we get a surjective $R$-algebra map $\rho:S\to S/\mathfrak q\cong\kappa$ with $\ker\rho=\mathfrak q$. Moreover: (*) two surjective $R$-algebra maps $\psi_1,\psi_2:A\to\kappa$ from an $R$-algebra $A$ with the same kernel are equal, because $\psi_2=\alpha\circ\psi_1$ for a ring automorphism $\alpha$ of $\kappa$ which is $R$-linear, and $\kappa$ is generated by $1$ as an $R$-module, so $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. In particular, for an $R$-algebra map $\tau:S\to R$ ($\tau\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_R$, so $\tau$ and $\pi\circ\tau$ are surjective) we have $\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\ker(\pi\circ\tau)$, and $\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q$ iff $\pi\circ\tau=\rho$.

*Standard etale presentation (Stacks: by Proposition 00UE).* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-locally-standard] applied to $R\to S$ and $\mathfrak q$ there are $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$, a monic $f\in R[t]$, an $h\in R[t]$ with $f'p_1+fp_2=h^n$ in $R[t]$ (some $p_1,p_2\in R[t]$, $n\ge0$) and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\varphi:S_g\xrightarrow{\sim}C=C(f,h)=R[t][Y]/(f,Yh-1)$; let $x\in C$ be the class of $t$ and $\lambda:S\to S_g$ the localization map. This is the only place where etaleness of $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is used.
